description: osrm is an R client for the Open Source Routing Machine service. Its functions request road routes, multi-stop trips, travel-time or distance matrices and isochrone polygons from a local or remote OSRM server, then return the results for analysis in R. The software uses the road network loaded into that server, commonly from OpenStreetMap; it contains no fixed regional road graph or historical time window. The JOSS paper points to a GitHub repository that now marks itself archived and directs readers to the current Codeberg project. The current R package DESCRIPTION says GPL version 3 or later, and its licence text is published there. This client can compute travel-time inputs for road-network simulations, compare accessibility after closures, or prepare origin-destination matrices. Its results depend on server profiles, map freshness and service limits; it does not simulate vehicle interactions or congestion by itself. The first-review draft model-osrm describes the separate C++ routing engine and does not include this R package. This review read both repository identities and the current package metadata, but did not start an OSRM server or send routing queries.
